title: The Three Languages
summary: A count sent his son to university for three years. The youth returned, having learned the language of barking dogs, the language of singing birds, and the language of croaking fro...
full_text:
A count sent his son to university for three years. The youth returned, having learned the language of barking dogs, the language of singing birds, and the language of croaking frogs!

Enraged, the father banished him. But the youth pacified ferocious guard dogs by understanding their hunger, retrieved buried gold, and listened to frogs prophesying that he would become the Pope in Rome!

In Rome, two white doves perched upon his shoulders, and the cardinals crowned him the supreme pontiff, fulfilling his destiny.
moral: Listening to the voices of nature prepares the humble soul for the highest office.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Three Languages"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.

author: Jacob & Wilhelm Grimm (1812–1857)
